derivation.source: one real mid-turn session on the operator's machine (~/.local-operator/sessions/<id>/transcript.jsonl, read-only copy). The session id is deliberately NOT recorded in this file; it is not needed by anything that reads the fixture.
derivation.transforms: (all stated in the fixture's `derivation`): journal truncated to the first JOURNAL_ROWS rows; `usage`/`provider_payload` narrowed to `duration_s` + `details`; `details` of `system_prefix`/`session_state`/`session_spend.v1` rows emptied (they project to nothing).
derivation.sanitization: EVERY text, argument, output, diff-line, path, range, url and handle string is a DETERMINISTIC LENGTH-PRESERVING PLACEHOLDER, not the real content (round 1, R2: the first version of this file carried the operator's real prompt, prose, git output and `~/...` paths into a public repository). Same original value -> same placeholder, so a path or handle repeated in the journal stays repeated; a diff line keeps its FIRST character, which is the only part `diffLineKind` reads; a scheme prefix (`spill://`, `guide://`, `skill://`, `session/`) is kept. LENGTHS ARE PRESERVED because the backend's own `_bound_live_events_in_place` chooses which `details` to strip by their cost against a per-frame share, so equal lengths keep the committed seed faithful to the derivation below. STRUCTURE IS UNTOUCHED: ids, ts, types, roles, call ids, tool names, ordering and `details.added/removed` are verbatim, and the fixture's own journal/live_events key shape and every string's length are identical to the pre-sanitization file.
derivation.correction: The earlier version of this note claimed text blocks and diffs were "truncated to 120 chars" and that tool_call argument strings were too. THAT WAS WRONG for the seed: `live_events[].result.content[].text` was never truncated by this fixture at all (it ran to 539 characters, bounded only by the backend's frame budget), and the claim was read as a promise about size that the file did not keep. Nothing depended on it: every assertion in `scripts/seed-label-gap.test.mjs` reads structure (ids, order, `details.added/removed`, non-empty output and diff), and the sanitization above now bounds the text by construction rather than by a truncation that did not happen.
